summary:
Normandie stands under France's national framework on transgender rights, which applies uniformly across all regions and departments. The source inventory contains no Normandie-specific transgender findings.

Within Normandie, the national custodial-inspection authority CGLPL carried out inspection visits at Caen prison as part of its opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty. That opinion, a follow-up to its opinion of 30 June 2010, records the persistence of serious violations of trans detainees' fundamental rights in adult prisons. The review covered the situations of some forty transgender detainees, with interviews including eight trans women and one trans man. No such violations were noted in mental-health establishments, closed educational centres or juvenile detention centres. The other inspection visits in the opinion were at Fleury-Mérogis, Saint-Martin-de-Ré and Toulouse-Seysses prisons and the Toulouse central police station, all outside Normandie.

The risks documented for transgender travellers in France concentrate in two settings: detention and the border. In everyday movement, accommodation and services, the country's own oversight bodies record persistent discrimination rather than legal prohibition.
tangentialFactors:
The CGLPL's 2021 opinion is a national instrument; its findings on adult prisons apply to Caen prison within Normandie as to any French establishment, while its finding that no violations were noted in mental-health establishments, closed educational centres or juvenile detention centres is likewise national in scope.

The opinion's inspection itinerary places Caen alongside Fleury-Mérogis, Saint-Martin-de-Ré and Toulouse-Seysses prisons and the Toulouse central police station, giving Normandie one of the five custodial sites examined.
localsOnly:
Trans detainees held in adult prisons in Normandie fall within the CGLPL's finding of persistent serious violations of fundamental rights, including placement by birth sex, isolation and exposure during strip searches, as recorded in its opinion of 25 May 2021.

Caen prison was one of the establishments inspected for that opinion, so conditions for trans detainees there were directly examined by the national preventive mechanism alongside interviews with some forty transgender detainees.
outOfScopeNotes: No Normandie-specific incident, enforcement action, or regional institutional practice involving transgender visitors or residents is documented in the inventory beyond Caen prison's inclusion in the CGLPL's inspection itinerary. Whether Caen prison has since implemented the CGLPL's binding guidance is unresolved in the sources provided.
